name: Urea
rangeNote: US labs usually report BUN (urea nitrogen) in mg/dL; many European labs report urea itself in mmol/L or mg/dL. Pick the matching unit.
summary: Urea is a waste product made by the liver when the body breaks down protein. The kidneys remove it.

high.meaning: A high urea can mean the kidneys are filtering less, but it also rises with dehydration and high protein intake.
commonCauses: Bleeding in the stomach or gut

low.meaning: A low urea is usually not a concern and often reflects low protein intake.

sources.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
